existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: Coverage has high-impact local R4-to-R6 breaks: mandatory `kind`, removal/split of required `payor`, and string-to-`Identifier` shape changes for `subscriberId` and `class.value`. The largest uncertainty is not whether these changes exist, but how official guidance expects ambiguous payer scenarios to migrate.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should first classify each Coverage as insurance, self-pay, or other; then map R4 `payor` to R6 `insurer` or `paymentBy`; then convert scalar string identifiers into `Identifier` objects. R6-to-R4 conversion is lossy for payer kind/responsibility, multiple or qualified identifiers, class identifier metadata, optional `statusReason`, `insurancePlan`, and expanded cost-to-beneficiary dimensions.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural differences because both assigned StructureDefinitions and package indexes were available locally and agree on identity. Confidence is medium for terminology and intent: most existing Coverage ValueSet compose definitions are unchanged, but expansions were not run and no official narrative diff or ConceptMap was supplied.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
Coverage keeps its resource identity. The aggregate has 4 hard R4-to-R6 instance break(s), 0 potential hard break(s), 2 non-mechanical migration finding(s), and 0 direct behavior/API finding(s).

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 2, which creates neutral stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 43/100, producing migration shape `moderate-targeted-remodel`, major migration `Partial`, and compatibility posture `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Expect targeted migration work, but continue reviewing individual breaks. Use less-breaking designs where they do not preserve obsolete or conflicting models indefinitely.

topFindings.title: Coverage.class.value changed from string to Identifier
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and runtime/API/codegen: R4 class entries with scalar `value` are not R6-shaped, and generated clients change from a string property to an Identifier object.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Coverage.subscriberId changed from a single string to repeating Identifier
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: the JSON type changes from a primitive scalar to repeating complex Identifier objects; R6-to-R4 loss is also possible for systems, assigners, periods, extensions, and extra repetitions.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Required R4 Coverage.payor was removed and split into insurer/paymentBy semantics
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and runtime/API/codegen: R4 JSON containing the required `payor` path is not an R6 Coverage, and client code, searches, mappings, and FHIRPath expressions using `Coverage.payor` must be rewritten.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Coverage.kind is a new mandatory required-code element with cross-element constraints
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 Coverage that otherwise maps forward lacks the required `kind` code, and generated R6 models also need a non-null discriminator value.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: R6 adds optional Coverage fields that are not natively representable in R4
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 instances using the new optional fields cannot be represented in plain R4 without extensions or loss, but this is not an old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 break.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Cost-to-beneficiary entries no longer require value[x] and gained additional benefit dimensions
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 can express cost components without `value[x]` or with additional dimensions that R4 cannot natively carry, but no R4-valid value on this path becomes R6-invalid.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Coverage.status semantics now explicitly separate resource status from policy in-force period
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: implementations that treated `active` as in-force may need business-rule changes, but the base element cardinality, type, modifier status, and required code family are not materially narrowed.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.
